question: If 6 men and 8 boys can do a piece of work in 10 days while 26 men and 48 boys can do the same work in 2 days, then the time taken by 20 men for doing the same piece of work will be:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Equating total work: (6 **men** + 8 **boys**) × 10 = (26 **men** + 48 **boys**) × 2

⇒ 30M + 40B = 26M + 48B ⇒ 4M = 8B ⇒ 1 **man** = 2 **boys**

Convert all to **men**: 6M + 8B = 6M + 4M = 10 **men**

If 10 **men** do the **work** in 10 days, then 20 **men** (double efficiency) will take half the **time**.

**∴ Time taken** = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Let the **efficiency** of one **man** be 'm' and one **boy** be 'b'.

 
 

 **Person/Group**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 Group 1 (6m + 8b)
 10
 10
 10 ÷ 10 = 1
 
 

 Group 2 (26m + 48b)
 2
 10 ÷ 2 = 5
 
 

⇒ 6m + 8b = 1 → (Equation 1)

⇒ 26m + 48b = 5 → (Equation 2)

To eliminate 'b', multiply (Equation 1) by 6: 36m + 48b = 6 → (Equation 3)

Subtracting (Equation 2) from (Equation 3):

⇒ (36m + 48b) − (26m + 48b) = 6 − 5

⇒ 10m = 1 ⇒ m = 1/10 (Efficiency of 1 **man**)

**Efficiency** of 20 **men** = 20 × m = 20 × (1/10) = 2 units/day

⇒ **Time taken** = **Total Work** ÷ **Efficiency** = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Man-Days Formula

The total **work** done is the product of **efficiency**, number of **persons**, and **time**: W = M × D × H × E.

Efficiency and Time Relationship

**Efficiency** is inversely proportional to **time** taken. If the number of workers is doubled, the **time** required to complete the same **work** is halved.

Group Work Comparison

When multiple types of workers (like **men** and **boys**) work together, always find the **efficiency ratio** between them to simplify the **calculation**.</p
